_doc: The brand palette, in one place. Everything else reads this file.
scripts/apply-brand-tokens.py rewrites the :root block in assets/css/style.css from
here, so a future rebrand is an edit to this file and one run, not a hunt through
2,500 CSS lines, 13 guide diagrams and three head-tag generators.
Every value below was measured, not chosen by eye. 'ratio_white' is the contrast
against #ffffff; anything a label sits on or is painted in must reach 4.5,
verify.py re-checks these, so a careless edit here fails the gate rather than
shipping a button nobody can read.

--brand.role: brand fill; white labels sit on this

--brand-deep.role: link ink and CTA gradient start

--gold.role: the mark's gold. DECORATION ONLY: never a label, never behind white text

--gold-deep.role: gold that has to carry text

--tint-bg.role: every informational chip, badge and quiet panel

--line.role: the rule above a page's byline and footer note; was never defined, so .page-foot drew its border-top in currentColor

unchanged: the status family (--danger, --warn) - teal is 128 points off red, so a failure still cannot be mistaken for brand
--maps-red, the Google Maps pin used once on the directory row

--text-inv.role: ink that sits ON the brand; the button label
